docs.title: Key differences from Jinja
docs.text:
• No template inheritance via strings — use component composition instead
  • Filters like {{ price | upper }} become JS methods: {price.toUpperCase()}
  • Static by default — renders to HTML at build time, no JS sent to browser unless you add <script> or a framework (React, Vue, etc.)
  • File-based routing — src/pages/services.astro → /services

docs.title: Dotfiles Repository Setup
docs.text:
Machine setup and sync, backed by telegit/dotfiles_2026.

Note

dotfiles/ lives nested inside this repo on disk for convenience, but it's tracked as a completely separate git repository with its own remote — it's git-ignored here, not a submodule.

docs.title: New Machine Setup
docs.text:
On a brand new Mac, run this one command:

bash <(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/telegit/dotfiles_2026/main/bootstrap.sh)

This will:

  • Install Homebrew
  • Install Oh My Zsh + Powerlevel10k
  • Clone the dotfiles repo
  • Install all software from Brewfile
  • Symlink dotfiles (.zshrc, .gitconfig, etc.)
  • Configure Git with your name/email
  • Create ~/projects directory
  • Install the new-python-project command
  • Install VS Code extensions

docs.title: Customization
docs.text:
Add more software to Brewfile:

echo 'brew "neovim"' >> dotfiles/Brewfile
echo 'cask "spotify"' >> dotfiles/Brewfile

Update Brewfile from the current machine's installed software:

cd ~/dotfiles
brew bundle dump --force

Add custom aliases to .zshrc:

vim ~/dotfiles/.zshrc
# Add your aliases
git add .zshrc
git commit -m "Add custom aliases"
git push

docs.title: Sync Between Machines
docs.text:
Pull latest dotfiles:

cd ~/dotfiles
git pull
source ~/.zshrc

Push dotfiles changes:

cd ~/dotfiles
git add .
git commit -m "Update configuration"
git push

docs.title: Maintenance
docs.text:
Keep software up to date:

brew update && brew upgrade

Update Brewfile after installing new software:

cd ~/dotfiles
brew bundle dump --force
git add Brewfile
git commit -m "Update Brewfile"
git push

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
If symlinks break:

cd ~/dotfiles
ln -sf ~/dotfiles/.zshrc ~/.zshrc
ln -sf ~/dotfiles/.gitconfig ~/.gitconfig
source ~/.zshrc

If the Powerlevel10k theme breaks:

p10k configure

If new-python-project isn't found:

cp ~/dotfiles/new-python-project.sh ~/.local/bin/new-python-project
chmod +x ~/.local/bin/new-python-project

docs.title: Night Owl Theme (iTerm2 + oh-my-zsh)
docs.text: Night Owl is a dark color theme by Sarah Drasner. It installs in two parts: the iTerm2 color preset (controls terminal colors) and the zsh theme (controls the prompt shape/layout).

docs.title: Step 1: iTerm2 Color Scheme
docs.text:
1. Download the color preset from nickcoutsos/nightowl-iterm2 (grab the NightOwl.itermcolors file)
  2. Import into iTerm2:
    • Open iTerm2 → Settings → Profiles → Colors
    • Click the Color Presets… dropdown → Import…
    • Select the downloaded NightOwl.itermcolors file
    • Choose Night Owl from the Color Presets dropdown

docs.title: Step 2: oh-my-zsh Theme
docs.text:
Night Owl isn't built into oh-my-zsh, so install it manually:

curl -o ~/.oh-my-zsh/themes/night-owl.zsh-theme \
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/macguirerintoul/night-owl-iterm2-zsh-theme/main/night-owl.zsh-theme

Then set it in ~/.zshrc:

ZSH_THEME="night-owl"

Reload your shell:

source ~/.zshrc

docs.title: Recommended Pairing
docs.text:
For the best Night Owl experience:

  • iTerm2 — Night Owl color preset (handles all colors)
  • zsh theme — night-owl or Powerlevel10k (handles prompt layout)
  • VS Code — Night Owl extension (search "Night Owl" by sdras)

Tip

The iTerm2 color preset does the heavy lifting. The zsh theme only controls prompt shape — the actual colors come from iTerm2.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
If colors look wrong:

  • Make sure Minimum contrast is set to 0 in iTerm2 color settings
  • Check that your terminal reports 256 colors: echo $TERM (should show xterm-256color)

If the zsh theme file is missing:

ls ~/.oh-my-zsh/themes/night-owl.zsh-theme
# Re-run the curl command above if not found

docs.title: Overview

docs.title: 1. NAS Mount Script
docs.text:
File: ~/mount-nas.sh

#!/bin/bash
MOUNT_POINT="/Volumes/stern-archive"

if ! mount | grep -q "$MOUNT_POINT"; then
    mkdir -p "$MOUNT_POINT"
    mount_smbfs "//noinefm_appuser@10.10.10.229/stern-archive" "$MOUNT_POINT"
fi

Make executable: 

chmod +x ~/mount-nas.sh

Store QNAP password in Keychain (run once): 

security add-internet-password -s 10.10.10.229 -a noinefm_appuser -w

Manual mount command: 

mount_smbfs "//noinefm_appuser@10.10.10.229/stern-archive" /Volumes/stern-archive

docs.title: 6. Future: Multiple Services with Caddy Reverse Proxy
docs.text: As more services are added to the Mac mini, use Caddy as a reverse proxy so everything is accessible via clean URLs on port 443 instead of raw ports.

docs.title: Install Caddy
docs.text: brew install caddy

docs.title: Caddyfile (~/ or /etc/caddy/Caddyfile)
docs.text:
Each service gets its own path: 

mac-mini {
    handle /noine-fm* {
        reverse_proxy localhost:5050
    }
    handle /other-app* {
        reverse_proxy localhost:5051
    }
}

docs.title: Run Caddy as a launchd service
docs.text: brew services start caddy

docs.title: Update Tailscale serve to point to Caddy (port 443) instead of individual app ports
docs.text: tailscale serve 443

docs.title: Pattern for adding a new service
docs.text:
1. Deploy app on a new port (5051, 5052, etc.)
  2. Create launchd plist for the app
  3. Add a handle block in Caddyfile
  4. Reload Caddy: brew services restart caddy

Generator function: Function that runs for a while, yields a value, and stops; next invocation causes execution to resume from same point until another value is yielded 

def ints(start, end):
  i = start
  while i <= end:
    yield i                                 # stop execution and returns i, until next invocation of ints
    i = i + 1
k = ints(1, 10)                             # return an instance of the generator function
while next(k):                              # iterate once and yields a value (Python 3: next(k), not k.next())
  print(k)
for j in ints(1, 10):                       # iterate until the function stops producing values
  print(j)

docs.title: Config File
docs.text:
This reads a named file, or by default looks for "(main_script.py).config.txt". It reads the file, throws away everything after a hash (either full-line or part-line comments), and splits on '='.

This can be called with config{}, which is loaded with default values. It can also be forced to accept only values for keys that are specified in the dictionary with at least one default, or to accept any key/value pair. Ints and bools are parsed accordingly.

By default, this code edits the dictionary in place, so if a default dictionary is passed in, it will be updated. It also returns the dictionary, in case none was passed in.

def read_config(filename = '', config = {}, limit_to_defaults = False): 

filename = filename if len(filename) > 0 else os.path.realpath(__file__).replace('.py', '.config.txt')
if not os.path.isfile(filename):
  return
with open(filename, 'r') as f:
  lines = f.read().splitlines()
  for line in lines:
    line = (line[:line.find('#')] if line.find('#') > -1 else line).strip()
    parameters = line.split('=')
    if len(parameters) != 2:
      continue
    key, value = (p.strip() for p in parameters)
    if limit_to_defaults and key not in config:
      pass
    value = True if isinstance(value, str) and value.lower() == 'true' else value
    value = False if isinstance(value, str) and value.lower() == 'false' else value
    value = int(value) if isinstance(value, str) and value.isnumeric() else value
    config[key] = value
return config

Then update the Google Fonts <link> in src/layouts/Base.astro to match.

docs.title: SEO — LocalBusiness Schema
docs.text:
JSON-LD structured data is auto-generated in Base.astro from site.ts. One LocalBusiness entry is output per location. No manual editing needed — just keep locations up to date in site.ts.

To verify: paste the live URL into Google's Rich Results Test.

docs.title: Contact Form Fields
docs.text: The form captures: name, email, phone (optional), dog breed (optional), dog age (optional), message. Fields are sent to Netlify Forms automatically. Add or remove optional fields in src/components/ContactForm.astro.
